methodology.transcript_scope: full transcript; not limited to overlapping speech
methodology.context_policy: Each response turn is assessed against up to 3 immediately preceding chronological turns; target may be any different speaker in that window.
methodology.moderator_policy: Moderation, introductions, summaries, follow-up questions, and repetition without a stance are uncertain; substantive stances are classified normally. Host identity is not used for classification.
methodology.overlap_policy: Overlap and interruption are not evidence of stance by themselves.
methodology.uncertain_policy: Every eligible response turn receives one record; unclear or non-stance turns are classified uncertain.
methodology.target_policy: Target is a specific earlier turn; no reverse inference. Response timestamp determines subtopic mapping.
limitations: ASR errors can affect stance and exact quote matching.
The analysis does not infer intent, ideology, bias, or factual correctness.

Good evening ladies and gentlemen. They say in politics there are no permanent friends or enemies, but when a compliment comes from the most unexpected quarters, it can create more ripples than the fiercest political attack. At a time when Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party are leaving no stone unturned in their offensive against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a voice from the very heart of the Gandhi family's inner circle has struck a remarkably different note. Sam Petroda, Rajiv Gandhi's trusted advisor, a Gandhi family confidant for decades on end, Rahul Gandhi's loyal lieutenant and guru, and the man who heads the Indian Overseas Congress, the very man gearing up to coordinate Rahul Gandhi's upcoming US visit. where the Congress leader is expected to renew his criticism of the Modi government at Columbia University no less. He has now showered lavish praise on Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Not a grudging acknowledgement, not a passing compliment, but a glowing account of Modi's personal warmth, kindness, affection and leadership qualities. And coming from one of Rahul Gandhi's most trusted men, the timing and the choice of words are particularly striking. Don't believe us? Well, listen in for yourselves. And Prime Minister Narendra Modi was quick to reciprocate with a personal touch on social media platform X. Addressing Petroda as Sam Bhai and his wife as Anjana Ben, he wrote and I quote, Happy Diwali and New Year Abhinandan. Praying for a joyful and healthy year ahead. Jai Jagannath. In fact, when a social media user cheekily asked, Sam Pitroda ko Diwali wish kar sakte hain, to humme bhi wish kar do, Modi ji. And the Prime Minister promptly replied, aapko bhi Happy Diwali, Mihir Bhai. And the warmth extended beyond social media. At the BJP's Diwali Milan, Prime Minister Modi fondly recalled his decades-old association with journalists. From political adversaries to old acquaintances, a reminder that political equations may change, ideological battles may intensify, but personal relationships and courtesies need not become casualties of political rivalry.

One day, a gang of journalists entered my room. At that time, there was a women's brigade. They had a lot of strength. They grabbed my neck. He said, give me sweets. I said, why? You didn't give me sweets. He said, are you going to Gujarat? Are you going to become the CM? I said, I don't know. He said, we all know that you are lying.

But here's the irony. Sonia Gandhi in her newly released memoir has presented a strikingly different portrait of Narendra Modi. She claims that despite over years of his prime ministership, they have had practically no real conversation. That when they come face to face, the prime minister offers a formal namaste but avoids eye contact. But since when did political courtesy come with an obligation of personal attention? Sonia Gandhi speaks of distance while her family's longtime confidant Sam Petroda speaks of warmth, affection and mutual respect. And if that contrast wasn't striking enough, Petroda's praise has now sparked a backlash within the opposition itself with a Congress leader who's even speculating about his political loyalty.
We don't live in this country, so we don't know what's going on there. That's why they must have said that they are thinking of killing us.

This is what even alliance partners are talking about Sam Petroda, a man so close to Mr Rahul Gandhi's heart. But this is hardly the first time Prime Minister Narendra Modi has demonstrated that political differences need not come in the way of personal courtesies. Remember his warm interaction with former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh at the inauguration of the Kartarpur Sahib corridor. Two political adversaries sharing a cordial moment despite years of ideological differences. honoring the position of a former prime minister or that emotional farewell to congress veteran Ghulam Nabi Azad in parliament itself. Modi broke down, wiped his tears and saluted Azad recalling their decades-old association when Gujarati Citizens had been affected by floods and Ghulam Nabi Azad as a Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir had helped out. Then there was that small but telling gesture towards Sharad Pawar. The Prime Minister helped the veteran leader with his chair and poured water for him. A simple act of courtesy despite their political differences. And even with Rahul Gandhi, his fiercest political rival, Modi has shared moments of cordiality. Remember their candid interaction at Prerna's Thal in Parliament, when they shared a lighter moment away from the political battlefield, and after Operation Sindoor when the Prime Minister reached out to leaders across party lines, meeting members of all party delegations who had taken India's message against terrorism to the world, Political differences set aside in national interest and perhaps the Prime Minister himself summed up this approach best when he reflected on years in public life.
